title: Memory leak in parseTimerConfig()-derived PendingEvent fields when PARALLEL_GATEWAY split emits multiple TIMER-created events in one transition
summary: Discovered incidentally while verifying the ISS-0091 (GitHub #343) migration-tracker-unification fix via zig build test-integration-iss203. Independent of ISS-0091 and not caused by it: tests/integration/iss203_idempotency_keys_test.zig's TC-ISS-203-01, TC-ISS-203-02, TC-ISS-203-04, and TC-ISS-203-05 all report Zig test-runner-detected memory leaks (DebugAllocator) traced to src/engine/transition.zig:1455 (parseTimerConfig's `try allocator.dupe(u8, duration_val.string)` for the ParsedTimerConfig.duration_iso8601 field) and, for TC-ISS-203-05 specifically (which uses a PARALLEL_GATEWAY split into two TIMER nodes, TIMER_A and TIMER_B), a larger 15-allocation leak also implicating src/engine/transition.zig:529 in the `transition()` PARALLEL_GATEWAY split path. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to the ISS-0091 fix: src/engine/transition.zig was not modified by that fix (only tests/integration/helpers.zig was), and the same leak trace appears identically whether or not the ISS-0091 fix is applied -- ISS-0091 only removes an earlier-in-the-test migration-tracking ServerError that was previously masking these tests from ever reaching the point where the leak is detected. All 5 ISS-203 test cases FAILED before the ISS-0091 fix (with the unrelated 'uq_form_schema_field already exists' migration error); after the fix, TC-01/02/04/05 fail only on the leak (TC-03 was not observed to leak in the runs performed). ownership of ParsedTimerConfig.duration_iso8601 / .repeat_expression transfers into PendingEvent.timer_created (see transition.zig:1080-1096), and from there into further downstream event-consumption code (outside transition.zig) that is expected to free it once the event has been persisted/reported -- the leak indicates some code path in that chain does not free these fields, most visibly when a single transition() call emits more than one TIMER-created event via a PARALLEL_GATEWAY split.

root_cause.details: src/engine/transition.zig::parseTimerConfig() allocates ParsedTimerConfig.duration_iso8601 (and optionally .repeat_expression) via allocator.dupe(). Ownership of these fields is moved into PendingEvent.timer_created (transition.zig:1088-1096) without any further dupe, so transition.zig itself does not double-own or leak them directly -- the leak must occur in whichever caller (in src/engine/instance.zig or a further downstream consumer of the emitted PendingEvent list) is responsible for freeing each PendingEvent's payload after it has been persisted to the events table / reported to the caller, and is not doing so for the timer_created variant, or not doing so in the PARALLEL_GATEWAY multi-timer fan-out case specifically. Not yet root-caused past this point -- full investigation of the PendingEvent lifecycle in src/engine/instance.zig is needed.

files_to_change: src/engine/instance.zig -- audit wherever the PendingEvent list produced by transition() is consumed/freed after being persisted; likely missing a free for .timer_created.duration_iso8601 / .repeat_expression / .payload_json in one or more code paths
src/engine/transition.zig -- not expected to need changes (ownership transfer at parseTimerConfig call sites appears correct), but re-verify once instance.zig's consumption side is understood

occurrences.context: Found while running zig build test-integration-iss203 to verify the ISS-0091 migration-tracker-unification fix. All 5 test cases leaked memory per the DebugAllocator; TC-ISS-203-05 (PARALLEL_GATEWAY split into 2 TIMER nodes) leaked 15 allocations. Confirmed present identically on baseline main (pre-ISS-0091-fix) and on the ISS-0091 fix branch -- unrelated to and not caused by the ISS-0091 change.

prevention: When a PendingEvent variant is added or its payload fields change ownership semantics, add or update a deinit/free helper covering every variant and call it from every code path that consumes the emitted events list, not just the primary single-event path -- multi-event fan-out cases (PARALLEL_GATEWAY split, etc.) are easy to under-test for cleanup because most hand-written unit tests exercise only a single emitted event.
